review_cost.rationale: Approve with nits: cancel the debounce timer, dedupe the route table, and two one-line cleanups. Nothing structural needs rework.

findings.issue: The 150 ms search-debounce timer is never cancelled when the user navigates away; if it fires after navigation, update() calls updateUrl(..., replace=true) (app/src/url-state.ts:25) which replaceState's the current history entry, leaving e.g. /pokemon/pikachu in the DOM with /?q=... in the URL, and markShown then records the wrong view.
findings.suggestion: Cancel the timer when the page's DOM is replaced, or guard the callback with isShown(locationKey()) before calling update(); both primitives already exist in url-state.ts.

findings.issue: The route table (path patterns + resource kinds) is duplicated between server.mjs RESOURCE_ROUTES/STATIC_ROUTES and main.ts ROUTES; adding or changing a route requires touching both or client and server disagree about 404s.
findings.suggestion: Extract the patterns into one shared module imported by both the client bundle and the server (plain .mjs re-exported from the TS side, or a JSON route table consumed by both).

findings.issue: Re-inlines the id-from-URL regex (Number(pokemon.url.match(/\/(\d+)\/?$/)?.[1])) instead of reusing idFromUrl from format.ts:19.
findings.suggestion: Import and use idFromUrl, which also returns NaN on no match instead of the implicit undefined→NaN here.

findings.issue: An out-of-range ?page= is clamped for display (Math.min(filters.page, totalPages)) but the URL still says e.g. page=999, so pagination links and the address bar disagree about the current page.
findings.suggestion: When the clamped page differs from filters.page, updateUrl to the normalized query (replace) so the URL matches the view.

findings.issue: pageStatus performs an upstream API fetch (3 s timeout) on every HTML navigation with no memoization, coupling every page's time-to-first-byte to API latency.
findings.suggestion: Cache 404 determinations per path with a short TTL, or document why the per-request check is preferred over always returning 200 (the spec makes 404 optional).

summary: A clean, genuinely idiomatic vanilla-TS/Vite SPA with excellent module boundaries, careful navigation-race handling, zero XSS surface, and the current stable toolchain. The one real bug is a leaked search-debounce timer that can corrupt the history entry after navigating away; the rest are small consistency nits (duplicated route table, one duplicated helper, a page-clamp/URL mismatch). I'd approve after the timer fix and route dedup — a round of small changes, no structural rework.
